summary: iter352 round-2 security-audit verification: 27/29 pass, 1 skipped (environment), 1 FAILING which is a real HIGH-severity bug in the R2-3 fix. Suite: /app/backend/tests/test_iter352_round2_audit.py. R2-1 cross-campus by-id 404: all 14 assertions pass — a Director scoped only to a fresh campus B gets 404 on GET /cases/{A}/notes, /cases/{A}/payments, /reviews/{A} (GET/PUT/DELETE), /members/{A}/profile-pdf, and still 200s on their own campus-B equivalents; admin still 200s on campus A. R2-2 privilege escalation via reset-password: Director→admin returns 403 with the exact 'You cannot reset the password of someone at your own level or above' message; admin login with the original password still works (verified after the attempt). Director→Member returns 200 and the member can log in with the new password. Admin→throwaway-admin returns 200 (throwaway admin created + deleted; the three real admins were not touched). R2-4 kiosk pin-checkin: action=lookup no longer returns date_of_birth on children (children carry only id/name/photo_url/family_id); per-IP throttle kicks in on ~20th call in 10 min. Per-socket safety-net test SKIPPED because the k8s preview ingress spread 300 spoofed calls across 300 distinct socket_ips — the code itself is present and correct in deps.py::enforce_public_rate_limit (limit*12 socket bucket), but this environment cannot pin a single socket. R2-5 kiosk unlock: unknown identifier and real+wrong-password both return the identical {'detail':'Invalid credentials'} 401; median timing deltas across 5 samples of each path are within the ratio threshold (dummy bcrypt burn on the not-found path is working). Valid PIN unlock still returns unlocked=true. Payslip PDF regression: owner + HR-same-campus + admin all 200, Director-of-other-campus 404. Real bug: R2-3 sibling-campus leak is NOT fully fixed — the failing test proves a Manager assigned only to a sub-location under campus A, after pinning the parent region, still sees campus B's data in the tenant listings.

critical.issue: R2-3 IS STILL BROKEN. A non-switcher Manager assigned ONLY to a sub-location under campus A, after PUT /api/user/active-campus with the parent region id, still sees campus B (sibling) data in campus-scoped list endpoints (verified against /api/events). Direct probe of get_campus_filter for `user={role:'Manager', location_id:'sub', location_ids:['sub','loc_002'], active_campus_id:'loc_001'}` returns a filter that includes loc_003 (sibling campus). Root cause: the parent-walk at the top of get_campus_filter (lines 340–347) climbs TWO levels for a sub-location user (sub → campus → region) and puts the region id into `user_loc_ids`. The iter351 restriction then computes `own_scope = user_loc_ids | expand_descendants(user_loc_ids)` — since user_loc_ids contains the region, expand_descendants walks the whole region and pulls every sibling campus into own_scope. Fix: compute own_scope from the ORIGINAL assignment (`user['location_id']` + `user['location_ids']` as stored, plus only their SUB-descendants), NOT from the parent-expanded set. Do the parent-walk only for the OTHER purposes (pin-target eligibility, feature access).

minor.issue: Cannot be verified in this preview: 300 spoofed X-Forwarded-For calls produced 300 distinct socket_ips (multi-replica ingress). The code path in deps.py::enforce_public_rate_limit is correct (per-socket bucket at limit*12), but end-to-end proof requires a fixed egress. Recommend testing behind a single proxy or asserting the DB shape (one socket_ip, hit count > limit*12) directly.

action_items: FIX (HIGH): backend/deps.py::get_campus_filter — recompute `own_scope` for the non-switcher parent-pin restriction using the user's ORIGINAL assignment (stored `location_id` + `location_ids`), not the parent-expanded `user_loc_ids`. Otherwise a Manager under a sub-location of any campus can pin the region and read every sibling campus's data. Suggested minimal patch: capture `original_user_locs = set(user.get('location_ids') or []) | ({user.get('location_id')} if user.get('location_id') else set())` BEFORE the parent-walk, and use `expand_descendants(original_user_locs, ...)` when computing `own_scope`.

rca of the issue: R2-3 (active-campus pin sibling leak) reproduction: (1) create a sub-location under campus A; (2) create a Manager assigned ONLY to that sub-location; (3) as the manager, PUT /api/user/active-campus {campus_id: <parent-region-id>}; (4) GET /api/events → response includes events from campus B (sibling of campus A). Root cause: at the top of deps.get_campus_filter, `user_loc_ids` is expanded by ONE parent hop per id via db.locations.find({id: {$in: user_loc_ids}, parent_id...}). Because the manager already has [sub, camp_a] stored (create_user resolves sub-location parents once), the parent hop climbs [sub→camp_a, camp_a→region] and lands loc_001 into user_loc_ids. The iter351 defensive block then does `own_descendants = expand_descendants(user_loc_ids)` — recursive — which from loc_001 fans out to every sibling campus (loc_002, loc_003) and every one of their sub-locations. own_scope thereby contains camp_b, and the intersection with the active-campus expansion doesn't clip it out. Mitigation: freeze the pre-walk assignment set (`original_locs = set(location_ids) | {location_id}`) and use it as the anchor for own_scope, so a user assigned to sub_of_camp_a's own_scope is at most {sub, camp_a, and camp_a's own descendants}, never sibling campuses. This preserves the ability to PIN the region (which set_active_campus already allows via a wider `parents` set) while restricting what pinning it can VIEW.
